{{Quote|See that little one I'm holding? His name was N'a-kee-tula, which means "sweetheart."|[[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], explaining a [[holograph]] featuring her and N'a-kee-tula to [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]]|<ref name="AOTC novel">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref>}}
'''Shadda-Bi''' was a [[Language/Legends|language]] of the [[Shadda-Bi-Boran (species)|Shadda-Bi-Boran]] [[Species/Legends|species]] on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Shadda-Bi-Boran/Legends|Shadda-Bi-Boran]].<ref name="TEA" /> The name [[N'a-kee-tula]] meant "sweetheart" in the language.<ref name="Insider">{{InsiderCite|80|The Unseen Planets of Episode II}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Shadda-Bi-Boran language was indirectly mentioned in a [[Content cut from Star Wars#Attack of the Clones|deleted scene]] from the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], written and directed by [[George Lucas]].<ref name="Deleted">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''</ref> The scene was included in the film's [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|novelization]] by [[R. A. Salvatore]],<ref name="AOTC novel" /> published on [[April 23]], [[2002]],<ref name="RandomHouse">{{RandomHouseOld|url=author/results.pperl?authorid=26771|text=R.A. Salvatore}}</ref> before the film's premiere on [[May 16]] later that year.<ref name="Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, Updated and Expanded Edition]]''</ref> The language was later identified as Shadda-Bi in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', a [[2009]] reference book written by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]].<ref name="TEA" />
